question: The selling price of 40 books is equal to the cost price of 28. Find the loss or profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: 40 × SP = 28 × CP

Ratio of SP to CP ⇒ SP / CP = 28 / 40 = 7 / 10

Let CP = 10 units and SP = 7 units.

Loss = CP − SP = 10 − 7 = 3 units.

Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100 = (3 / 10) × 100 = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 40 books = Cost price of 28 books

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100

 
 
 
•

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price (CP) of 1 book be ₹1.

⇒ Total CP of 40 books = ₹40.

⇒ Total Selling price (SP) of 40 books = CP of 28 books = ₹28.

⇒ Since SP is less than CP, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss on 40 books = CP − SP = 40 − 28 = ₹12.

⇒ Loss % = (Loss / Total CP) × 100

⇒ Loss % = (12 / 40) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 3 × 10 = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP. Loss occurs when CP > SP. Loss = CP − SP.

Profit/Loss Percentage Formula

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the base of the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a trader sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, the actual cost price is based on the false weight given. Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
